The '''Resistance Songbook''' was an underground Belcantese compilation of traditional and newly composed songs preserved during Vesperan occupation. Source material dates its compilation to 1920-1945.

== Role ==

The songbook helped maintain the [[Belcantese Language]] when public Belcantese education and performance were restricted. Songs carried local history, place memory, family teaching, political warnings, and coded resistance messages.

== Cultural Importance ==

Belcantese identity was strongly tied to song, so preserving music also preserved political memory. The songbook became one of the most important symbols of the [[Belcantese Cultural Resistance]].

== Postwar Legacy ==

After independence, the songbook helped restore public Belcantese culture. Language teachers, musicians, and historians treated it as evidence that occupation had failed to erase Belcantese identity.
